newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady to down despite cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady to down despite cold.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to lower Thursday in sluggish activity, with low sulphurs still pressured by oversupply despite the approach of an Arctic cold wave on the East Coast, industry sources said.
"Rack demand has been pretty good, but we still haven't seen much utility demand," said one cash trader, adding oversupply of some grades continued to weigh on the complex.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped another 25-50 cents to about the $17.75 a barrel level, with February paper off a similar amount to about $17.50, traders said.
While the cold may help trim some inventories, traders said it would take a sustained wave to trim stocks and stir better utility interest.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also remained under pressure, off 25 cents or more to about $18.50.
High sulphurs in New York again held relatively steady.
U.S. Gulf one percent skidded 50 cents to about $17 on reports 100,000 barrels sold late Wednesday at $17.10. USG three percent was 25-50 cents lower at about $15.50.
A Florida utility tendered for 110,000 barrels of 2.2 percent or 100-180,000 barrels of 1.8 percent for delivery by Feb 28. Bids are due Friday at 1000 EST.
New York city gate swing gas prices jumped more than $1 Thursday to above $6.00/mmBtu on the upcoming cold. NYH one percent resid was at a $2.82/mmBtu equivalent.
